title: Grateful Dead Live at Auditorium Theatre on 1971-08-23

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of the August 23 1971 Chicago show, with high‑energy performances and smoking The Other One/Cryptical suite.
ai_review.review: The Miller SBD transfer is praised for its clarity and faithful mix, letting the band's summer‑'71 fire shine through.  Highlights include a monster Cryptical Envelopment → Uncle → The Other One sequence, tight Phil Lesh bass work, and rare Pigpen moments, while a few sloppy spots (Promised Land’s “train‑wreck” ending) are noted.  Overall the show is regarded as one of the strongest from that tour.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews are 4‑5 stars, emphasizing both superb musical performance and a clean soundboard source; only a handful of lower or unrelated ratings temper the average slightly.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Multiple reviewers cite a great transfer, crisp clarity and no major drop‑outs; the SBD source is clean and well‑balanced.

standout_songs: The Other One (Cryptical Envelopment → Uncle suite)
China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: Two long sets (~28 songs, 3¼ hr) that blend new material with classics; the second set builds a high‑energy arc around the Cryptical/Uncle/Other One sandwich and finishes strong with Wharf Rat and an extended Good Lovin'.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Noted playing a Telecaster on this night; his lead work is described as smooth and excited, especially in the The Other One suite.
band_member_comments.Phil: Repeatedly praised for ‘popping off’ on lead‑bass, delivering mad‑man eighth‑note runs that drive the show.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mentioned as part of the The Other One transition; no specific critique beyond standard Dead drumming.
